text: Welcome to the capstone. Everything in this course has been taught in pieces. Now you'll combine it into one continuous project: two dashboards for one company, ending in a presentation and a portfolio write-up. You'll apply, not relearn: report types, filters, formulas, charts, and dashboard filters.

The company is Harborline Supply Company, a fictional industrial-supplies distributor with about 180 employees, running Sales Cloud and Service Cloud in one org. Every figure here is an illustrative example. Your Developer Edition or sandbox data will differ, and that's fine, because what matters is the method. Your boss, the VP of Revenue Operations, wants a sales dashboard for Monday and a service dashboard for Thursday.

Sales first. Five questions. Are we on track against a six million dollar quarterly quota? How much open pipeline covers the gap? How does closed revenue split across West, Central and East? What are our win rate and average deal size? And which open deals have gone quiet? Notice that each question is measurable, and each has someone who will ask it every week.

Then service. How many cases opened and closed this month? Is the backlog growing? How many high-priority cases are old or escalated? Where do cases come from? And how is work spread across the twelve agents? Same method, different object.

Here's the example baseline to check your work. Closed won so far: three point nine million from 81 deals, sixty-five percent of quota. Open pipeline: four point two million, two times coverage. On service: 1,840 opened, 1,725 closed, and a backlog of 412, up 115.

Both dashboards follow the same five steps. Write the question. Choose the report type. Build the report with filters and formulas. Choose the chart. Assemble the dashboard with filters and a sensible running user, then check every number against its source report. Each report answers exactly one question. Before you start, use a Developer Edition org or a sandbox with sample data, and create a folder for your work. Name everything clearly, since naming is part of being trustworthy.
Next up: build the sales dashboard, step by step.
